_note: Public model providers the privacy gateway may use, in order. Every request is redacted first. The first entry uses the caller's own key (the Dahl key the caller sends). A fallback needs enabled=true, a model, and a key FILE NAME under D:\jarvis-secrets (the key itself never goes in this file). Free tiers change: check the provider's current terms (jarvis/docs/reports/evidence/06-models-hardware-providers.md section 9). Gemini's free tier is excluded for personal data (its terms allow training on it).

providers.name: dahl
providers._note: A caller that sends its own key gets that key through (the plugins do). A caller that sends none, or the placeholder jarvis-local (the face does), gets the key in D:\jarvis-secrets\providers\dahl.key; if that file is missing the request goes out as it came and Dahl answers 401. The gateway hides the reasoning of a reply to the face (reasoning_content and <think> text). OPTIONAL, off until checked live: rename _face_extra_body_example to face_extra_body (or to extra_body for every caller) to ask Dahl to skip the thinking for the GLM default model, or _face_extra_body_example_deepseek (same way, pin the gateway's model to deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 first with D:\jarvis-secrets\gateway-pin.txt so the request actually reaches that model) for DeepSeek's own documented switch. Whether DAHL (the aggregator JARVIS actually calls, not the model's own vendor) forwards either field through to the model unchanged is NOT verified; a provider that does not know it may answer 400 naming the field, then remove it.
providers._speed_note_2026_10_26: D60. Read from the vendors' own pages on 2026-10-26: Dahl's API page (inference.dahl.global/docs/api/) documents model, messages, stream, tools/tool_choice and says some non-standard parameters are rejected with an error that names them; it documents NO thinking switch (not enable_thinking, chat_template_kwargs, reasoning_effort or thinking), and its models page lists zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash as a reasoning model and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 as 'fast model for coding, reasoning, and agents', MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7 without a reasoning note. MiniMax's own OpenAI-compatible page (platform.minimax.io) says that for M2.x 'thinking cannot be disabled' (a thinking:{type:disabled} is accepted and ignored) and that thinking tokens count toward max_tokens; only the M3 family takes thinking:{type:disabled}. So no switch is verified for either model and none is on. To try one on the laptop: rename _face_extra_body_example to face_extra_body, send one goal, and read /health latency_ms first_ms before and after (HTTP 400 naming the parameter = Dahl rejects it: remove it). Do the same for _face_tool_max_tokens_example (a small max_tokens on the face's tool-carrying requests): safe only if thinking is off, because a reasoning model spends the same limit on its hidden thinking and may answer with nothing.
providers._speed_note_2026_10_27: D80, re-checked the same way (D44) on 2026-10-27, nothing here turned on. MiniMax's own docs, re-read today: unchanged, M2.x (which covers MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2.7, the model Dahl marks default) still cannot disable thinking ('Accepted but ignored; thinking remains on'); only the separate MiniMax-M3 and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash models can (M3: 'skips thinking and answers directly'; M3.1-Flash: sending disabled returns 400), and Dahl's OWN models page does not list either M3 model today, so this path stays closed on Dahl specifically. GLM's own docs (docs.z.ai, GLM-5 page, today) DO document a real switch for GLM-5 itself: a `thinking` object with `type` 'enabled' (default) or 'disabled', same shape as GLM-4.6's; the page does not name GLM-5.3 or a Flash variant by name, so whether zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (Dahl's listing) takes the exact same field is a reasonable guess from the shared family, not confirmed. _face_extra_body_example above was corrected from a `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` guess (that key is a self-hosted vLLM/transformers convention, not what GLM's own hosted API documents) to this `thinking` shape. DeepSeek's own API reference (api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion, today) is the clearest find: `reasoning_effort` accepts `none` ('disables thinking mode'), `low`, `high`, `max` (default `high`), and a separate `thinking.type` accepts `enabled`/`disabled`; the guide's own example for model id `deepseek-flash` (deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 is the model Dahl lists under that family) sends both fields together. Both parameter names were already accepted by this gateway's own `_control_ok` validator before today (reasoning_effort's word list already includes 'none'), so no gateway code changed for this; only the example above and this note did. None of the three vendor pages says anything about what DAHL ITSELF (the aggregator inference.dahl.global, not z.ai or deepseek.com) forwards or rejects for an unlisted field: Dahl's own API page, re-read today, is unchanged from 2026-10-26 (still names only model/messages/stream/tools/tool_choice, still warns a non-standard parameter is rejected with a NAMED error, still does not mention `thinking` or `reasoning_effort` at all). So the switch most likely to work AS DAHL ACTUALLY SERVES IT today is `_face_extra_body_example_deepseek` (reasoning_effort: none) tried against deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 specifically (pin the gateway to it first), because that is the one model+field pair with a FULL vendor-documented round trip (DeepSeek's own docs name the exact model id and the exact field); GLM's is the next best guess; MiniMax-M2.7 (the default) has no switch at all, documented or not. Sources (2026-10-27): https://inference.dahl.global/docs/api/ , https://inference.dahl.global/docs/models/ , https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api , https://docs.z.ai/guides/llm/glm-5 , https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/reasoning_model , https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion
